summary: Richard O. Meisezahl (1906–1992) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Bonn in 1944. He served as an assistant there from 1945 to 1947 and founded the International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies.

Richard P. Boyle studied under Joshu Sasaki and earned his Ph.D. from Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa in 1982, completing postdoctorates at Düsseldorf and Washington University in St. Louis. He was an associate professor at Oregon Health & Science University (1986–2000).

Richard P. Hayes is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Toronto (1972–1982) under Bimal Krishna Matilal, later serving on the faculties of McGill University (1988–2003) and the University of New Mexico (2003–2013).

Richard Payne is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as Dean of the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1996, 2007) and held affiliations with the University of Chicago (attested 2021) and Numata Center (attested 2026).
Richard Peter Hottelet is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Narayan Hemandas Samtani. He held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, attested in 1971.

Richard Phené Spiers (1838–1916) worked in history and archaeology. He studied at King's College London from approximately 1854 to 1858 and subsequently at the École nationale supérieure des beaux-arts from around 1858 to 1861.

Richard Pischel (1849–1908) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. and habilitation at the University of Breslau, studying under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He held professorships at Halle-Wittenberg (1885–1902) and the Humboldt University of Berlin (1902–1908).

Richard Polenberg (1937–2020) was a historian who earned his B.A. at Brooklyn College and his Ph.D. at Columbia University. He served as Professor of American History at Cornell University from 1966 to 2011 and as a Fulbright Visiting Professor at Hebrew University (1980–1981).

Richard S. Cohen works in Buddhist studies and religious studies, having studied under Walter M. Spink and Luis Oscar Gómez. He serves as Associate Professor of South Asian Religious Literatures at the University of California, San Diego.

Richard Schechner (born 1934) studied at Cornell University, the University of Iowa, and Tulane University. Beginning around 1967, he served as a University Professor at New York University's Tisch School of the Arts.

Richard Scherzl (born 1850) was a linguist educated at Charles University, Saint Petersburg State University, and the University of Kharkiv. He served as director at Odesa University (1886) and held docent and professor positions in Latin at Kharkiv between 1882 and 1894.

Richard Schmidt (1866–1939) was an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. and habilitation at Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He served as librarian for the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (1904–1910) and professor at the University of Münster from 1910.

Richard Shilleto (1809–1876) was a scholar in linguistics. He was educated at Repton School and Shrewsbury School before completing his studies at Trinity College, Cambridge, from approximately 1828 to 1832.

Richard Simon (1865–1934) was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel and studied under Ernst Windisch, Edmund Hardy, and Albrecht Weber. He served as Privatdozent (1892) and extraordinary professor (1906) at the University of Munich.

Richard Sorabji (born 1934) is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at Pembroke College, Oxford. He held academic posts at Cornell University (circa 1962–1970), King's College London (circa 1970–2000), and Gresham College (circa 2000–2006).

Richard Sproat (born 1960) is a computational linguist who earned his Ph.D. from MIT in 1985. His career includes posts at Bell Labs (1985–1999), the University of Illinois (2003–2009), Oregon Health & Science University (2009–2012), Google, and Sakana AI (2024).

Richard Stothert (1833–1898) was an Indologist educated at the University of Glasgow and the University of Edinburgh, where he earned an M.A. He served as Principal of Wilson College, Mumbai, from 1876 to 1884.

Richard Sylvan (1935–1996) was a philosopher who studied at Victoria University of Wellington and Princeton University. He held academic posts at the University of Sydney from around 1963 to 1965 and as a fellow at the Australian National University beginning in 1971.

Richard Taupier works in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctorate and MS at the University of Massachusetts Amherst, where he served as Associate Director of Research Development, alongside teaching at Smith College.

Richard W. Lariviere (born 1950) is an Indologist who earned a Sanskrit doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher. He served as dean at UT Austin, provost at the University of Kansas, president of the University of Oregon, and Field Museum president.
